sense: to keep something in your mind

pins.definition: To keep something in your mind or bring a past fact or event back to mind.
To have or bring back a memory of someone or something from the past.
To have someone or something in your memory; not to forget.

situation: An elderly woman sits quietly at her kitchen table while a faded childhood photograph floats suspended inches above her palm, glowing softly with warm light as if projecting its memory into the room.
subject: the preserved memory
brief: An elderly woman sits at a wooden kitchen table holding her palm upward, and hovering just above her skin is a luminous, fully-colored miniature garden path from a decades-old photograph, glowing softly against the dim room. The rest of the kitchen is ordinary and quiet, untouched, while the small floating scene shines brightly as the clear focal point of her gaze.
prompt: An elderly woman sits at a wooden kitchen table holding her palm upward, and hovering just above her skin is a luminous, fully-colored miniature garden path from a decades-old photograph, glowing softly against the dim room. The rest of the kitchen is ordinary and quiet, untouched, while the small floating scene shines brightly as the clear focal point of her gaze. surrealism in the manner of Magritte and Dalí, one impossible juxtaposition rendered with complete photographic conviction, still air, an empty horizon. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
